# Results — Study 771 (Box-Office-Bomb)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **sell
Disney (DIS) after a notorious box-office flop weekend**: a nine-figure bomb should sag the
studio's stock once the disappointing weekend is public. Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the
last complete calendar month). Fingerprint `f3ff7b3017ec` (DIS + SPY, one combined panel,
adjusted/total-return daily closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `DIS` (Disney) + `SPY` (S&P 500), one combined panel: 4,147 rows, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 16 notorious Disney box-office bombs 2012→2025, real wide-release opening dates (Box Office Mojo / studio releases). *Dark Phoenix* & *West Side Story* are ex-Fox titles released after Disney's 2019 acquisition — their losses hit Disney's P&L |
| Anchor | first trading session on/after the **Monday after opening** — the first session at which the flop weekend is common knowledge (weekend estimates print Sunday, actuals Monday). Calendar-known, zero look-ahead |
| Events resolvable | all **16** of 16 flops have DIS+SPY coverage around the anchor |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the abnormal return (DIS − SPY) across independent, non-overlapping flop events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut; leave-one-out jackknife |
| Execution / costs | post-flop = [anchor → anchor+K]; the trade is a **short** (sell the studio), reported net of 2× one-way cost × NAV. Gross AND net reported |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) for both legs |

**Why the prior is skeptical:** a single flop, even a $200M write-down, is a rounding error
for a ~$200bn conglomerate whose revenue is dominated by parks, ESPN, streaming and consumer
products. A known, scheduled disappointment is exactly what a semi-strong-efficient market
should already price. So the desk expects a non-event.

## The post-flop — abnormal return, K sessions AFTER the anchor (DIS − SPY)

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | up rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week post (k=10) | 16 | **−1.034%** | **−1.533** | 9/16 = 56.2% [33.2%, 76.9%] |
| 1-month post (k=21) | 16 | **−1.767%** | **−1.622** | 7/16 = 43.8% [23.1%, 66.8%] |

The folklore points the right way: after a notorious flop DIS does *under*-perform SPY, by
−1.03% over two weeks and −1.77% over a month, and both cuts carry a negative *t*. But
neither clears the significance bar (|*t*| ≈ 1.5–1.6, well short of the desk's ~2.5), and the
up-rate is a coin-flip. This is a whiff of a real tilt, not a clean signal.

## The pre-release drift (context) — K sessions BEFORE the anchor

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | up rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week pre (k=10) | 16 | +0.001% | +0.001 | 10/16 = 62.5% [38.6%, 81.5%] |
| 1-month pre (k=21) | 16 | −1.109% | −0.809 | 8/16 = 50.0% [28.0%, 72.0%] |

No pre-release run-up to speak of: the two-week pre window is a dead zero and the one-month
pre is a weak, insignificant sag. Whatever underperformance exists is concentrated *after*
the flop is public — consistent with the "sell the news" framing, just not strongly.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event)

| cut | tail | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week post | left | −1.034% | −0.117% (0.949%) | 0.169 |
| 1-month post | left | −1.767% | −0.245% (1.422%) | 0.139 |

The observed post-flop sag sits in the **left half but not the tail** of the luck cloud:
~14–17% of random DIS-vs-SPY windows of the same length are at least this negative. (Note
the placebo mean is itself slightly negative — DIS lagged SPY over 2010–2026 — so part of
the raw −1% is just Disney's ordinary drag, not a flop effect.) Not distinguishable from
noise at any conventional level.

## Jackknife (leave-one-out) — 2-week post-flop *t*

Full-sample *t* = **−1.533**; across all 16 leave-one-out draws the *t* stays in
**[−1.801, −1.088]** — always negative, so the sag is **not** one bad film driving
everything; it's a broad, shallow, insignificant tilt.

## Tradability — the SHORT (sell the studio) net of costs

| window | gross DIS−SPY | SHORT net @ 5 bps | SHORT net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week post | −1.034% (*t* −1.53) | +0.934% (*t* +1.38) | +0.834% (*t* +1.24) |
| 1-month post | −1.767% (*t* −1.62) | +1.667% (*t* +1.53) | +1.567% (*t* +1.44) |

Flipping the sign (you *short* DIS, so a −1% window is a +1% short P&L) the trade earns
about +0.9–1.7% per event gross of nothing, but with *t* ≈ 1.4–1.5 it is not statistically
distinguishable from zero, it fires 16 times over 13 years (a capacity- and borrow-trivial
curiosity), and it lives inside a 4-window / 2-horizon search. Nothing to bank.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (drop = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = +0.07 (sd 1.03); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **0/20** seeds —
  the detector is quiet on the null at this n.
- **Planted post-flop drop −1.0% (seed 773):** mean AR −0.12%, *t* = −0.14.
- **Planted post-flop drop −2.0% (seed 773):** mean AR −1.12%, *t* = −1.35 — the planted
  sell-off is recovered monotonically (a −3% plant clears |*t*| > 1.5). At n = 16 with a
  10-day AR the machinery needs a *large* real drop to reach significance, which frames why
  the observed −1% shows up only as a whiff.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **Weak** | The sign is the folklore's: DIS under-performs SPY after a flop at both horizons (−1.03% / −1.77%), and the jackknife keeps *t* negative on every leave-one-out. But |*t*| ≈ 1.5–1.6 is short of significance, the placebo p is 0.14–0.17 (inside the luck cloud), the up-rate is a coin-flip, and part of the raw sag is just Disney's decade-long drag vs SPY. Directionally consistent but not robust. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Mirage** | Nothing to bank. The short earns ~+0.9–1.7% per event with *t* ≈ 1.4–1.5 (insignificant), fires 16 times in 13 years, is borrow-/capacity-trivial, and sits inside a multi-window search. |

**In one sentence:** selling Disney after a notorious flop points the right way — the stock
does mildly lag the market in the weeks after a bomb — but the effect is too small and too
noisy (|*t*| ≈ 1.5, placebo p ≈ 0.15) to distinguish from Disney's ordinary underperformance,
and there is no tradable edge in a 16-event, once-a-year curiosity.
